## Historical audit — S0163

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible; the supplied observations through JSONL line 24 are complete lines, not split observations.

| Area | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The instructed goal was a single-RGB indoor reconstruction with separate editable meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusions. The student interpreted the image as a shipboard sleeping and machinery compartment; that scene identity and depth are interpretations, not independently verified facts (lines 1, 3). |
| Initial construction | The first program created distinct room, three-tier bunk, column, equipment, chair, bench, fixture and overhead-service assemblies. It used colored primitives, material roughness and emission, rather than an observed texture pattern. Bunk rails and posts were grouped and positioned to meet, but physical connection and visual correctness were not independently checked. The static scene has no articulated pose to validate (lines 3–4). |
| Validation and exploration | Step 1 executed successfully and the runner saved a render and blend file (line 5). Given reference and render images, the student independently reported a cropped column foot, absent vent and hidden fixtures, and pale machinery; it diagnosed local placement/occlusion and lighting rather than camera error. These are student visual judgments, not independent image verification (lines 8–10). The sessions report zero student tool calls; exploration occurred through generated programs, runner executions and image-review turns (lines 2, 9). |
| Executed revisions | Step 2 moved and enlarged the column, moved the vent, lamp and wall fixtures, altered the bunk front post and connected rails, and lowered frontal fill while retaining the camera. It executed successfully and saved another render (lines 14, 16–17). The student judged step 2 better, but still identified aisle, foreshortened-board and brightness residuals (line 22). |
| Latest visible action | The third program moved the column forward, shortened the bunk and lengthened its uprights, added a transverse fixture bulkhead, and set exposure to −0.85; the runner invoked step 3 (lines 22, 24). No step-3 execution result or final selection is visible. Select events alternate between steps 1 and 2, so they do not establish the final submitted output (lines 18–19, 23). |
| Teacher | No separate teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update appears in the visible portion. The audit and revisions are the student’s own, prompted by the reconstruction workflow; no teacher receipt or adoption can be established. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Two builds formally rendered successfully; overall reconstruction quality and final outcome remain **unknown**, not formal scene success or algorithm failure. The images themselves are not supplied to this audit, so object visibility, material appearance, part contact, camera match and lighting discrepancies cannot be independently verified. The proposed bulkhead and exposure change were executed as code, but their rendered effect is unknown.

**Lessons.** Transferably, separate local geometry, camera and illumination hypotheses and compare rendered results before attributing improvement. Here, moving the column and reorienting the board are task-specific hypotheses; whether they restore the intended negative space or introduce new occlusion remains unresolved.
